title: Flap Track Fairing — Removal and Attachment Lug Examination

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of a flap track fairing with the flaps supported on jacks, and examination of the attachment lug and the drain provision that together decide whether the fairing may be refitted.

sections.purpose: This task removes a flap track fairing so that the track, the carriage or the fairing attachment can be reached, and examines the attachment lug and the drain for the condition that has grounded aircraft in tropical service.
sections.job_setup_note: The flaps must be fully extended and on jacks. A fairing removed with the flaps on hydraulic pressure alone has killed people. Have the crack finding procedure available before you start: if a lug crack is found, the fairing must not be refitted and Aeralis must be informed before the aircraft moves.
sections.procedure: 1. Extend the flaps fully and support them on jacks in accordance with the maintenance manual. WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER AN EXTENDED FLAP THAT IS NOT ON JACKS. RESIDUAL PRESSURE WILL RETRACT IT. 2. Position the fairing support trestle under the fairing in zone 564, 654 or 662 as applicable. 3. Photograph the fairing in position and note the clearance at the four measurement points. 4. Release the aft attachment and support the fairing. CAUTION: RELEASE THE AFT ATTACHMENT LAST WHERE THE SINGLE LUG IS FITTED. THE FAIRING WILL PIVOT ON THE FORWARD ATTACHMENT AND STRIKE THE TRACK. 5. Release the forward attachment and lower the fairing onto the trestle. 6. Clean the attachment lug and do a detailed visual inspection under a light of at least one thousand lux. 7. Where any crack indication is found, stop, photograph it with a scale in frame and inform Aeralis before the aircraft is moved. 8. Where the twin-lug arrangement is fitted, check both spherical bearings for play and for grease loss. 9. Examine the drain: where the moulded fitting is fitted, confirm that it stands proud of the sealant land and is clear; where the drilled hole is used, confirm that it has not been closed by paint. 10. Examine the inside of the fairing for standing water marks and for corrosion at the lower joint. 11. Check the actuator assembly D2750136872416 and the transmitter 339CE7 on the track for security. 12. Check the solenoid 984CE in the outboard position and its harness for chafe against the fairing. 13. Cover the fairing aperture if the fairing will be off for more than one shift.
sections.close_out: Record the clearance at the four measurement points before removal, the lug condition, the drain state and any standing water evidence. Where a crack is found, do not refit the fairing and quote this task in the report to Aeralis.

type_data.effectivity_note: SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft; steps 4, 8 and 9 differ between the single-lug and twin-lug standard

safety_precautions: Support the flaps on jacks before any work.
Do not release the forward attachment first on a single-lug fairing.
Use a light of at least 1 000 lux for the lug inspection.
